To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a resource bounded agent must be able to use plans as a means of limiting the amount of practical reasoning that it does, (ii) plans are best understood as being the product of an iterative, means end reasoning process, and (iii) the process of plan formation is best understood as a process that involves the interaction of means end reasoning and plan execution
(1) a rational agent must have a set of plans that (2) constrain her practical reasoning, (3) in a way that is sensitive to resource constraints.

the architecture of a resource bounded rational (RBRA) agent is a hybrid architecture, and that the practical reasoning component (PRC) of such an agent is a plan-based, means-end reasoning mechanism that is resource bounded.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to design an architecture that will allow a resource bounded rational to act effectively in the face of a changing and uncertain environment.
the problem of providing an adequate account of the role of plans and goals in the reasoning of rational agents.
the development of an architecture for rational agents that is capable of performing both means end reasoning and the weighing of competing goals and alternatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the practical reasoning of a rational agent is plan and resource bounded.
a rational agent is a planning agent.
the practical reasoning component is an important part of a theory of action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the agent's plans serve as a kind of "meta-logic" for her practical reasoning, and that this meta-logic can be implemented by a resource bounded agent.
the architecture we present here is an attempt at a formalization of the notion of bounded rationality.
the agent is able to reason about the world, and the world is able to reason with the agent, but the agent is not able to reason about her own reasoning.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the architecture of a practical reasoning system should be designed so as to take advantage of the structure of the agent's environment, and so as to take into account the fact that the agent is resource bounded.
practical reasoning can be seen as a form of means end reasoning, and that this form of reasoning is best carried out in a plan based manner.
a rational agent's reasoning is not only bounded by the resources she has, it is also bounded by the plans she has.
